content: Nonalcoholic Fatty Liver Disease (NAFLD) and Nonalcoholic Steatohepatitis (NASH) are conditions that can lead to liver fibrosis, and accurate assessment of fibrosis risk is critical for proper management. For patients who have indeterminate or high FIB-4 scores, it is recommended to measure liver stiffness using elastography techniques. This approach helps to stratify the risk of fibrosis with greater precision. A liver stiffness measurement (LSM) of 0 kPa is associated with a low risk of fibrosis. However, liver stiffness measurement using elastography is not widely accessible in all clinical settings. In such cases, specialists may consider alternative diagnostic tools, such as the Enhanced Liver Fibrosis (ELF) test, to evaluate the degree of fibrosis. These alternative methods can provide valuable insights when elastography is unavailable.
